notes:
40 stations, numbered 121–160 with no gaps, all under the section heading WEST COAST OF ENGLAND. There are no sub-headings, so coast is 'West Coast of England' on every row.

Conventions used:
- Fragments are each printed line exactly as it appears, with only the leading indentation removed. The trailing period on the number is kept in the fragment but left off in `number`.
- `keepers` holds only the personal names. Roles printed after a name ('P. K.', presumably principal keeper; 'mate'; 'gunner') go in `other`. Where a station names two people, `other` adds the name in brackets so it is clear whose role it is: these bracketed names are my own wording, not printed text.
- `other` may join two separately printed pieces with '; '.
- Light descriptions (colour, fixed/revolving, ray) go in `character`. Heights go in `other`. The exceptions are 150 Bideford, where colour and height are mixed in one phrase so the whole phrase is in `character`, and 144 Nash (High), where the whole three-light description is in `character`.

Asterisks: I count 23 (121–127, 129, 131, 132, 134, 137, 138, 144, 146, 147, 149, 150, 152, 153, 155, 156, 159), which matches the other reader's count. The text says 24 returns. The list alone can't show which station is missing its asterisk. One guess is 139 Milford (High): the report treats it as one station with 138 and the same keeper, G. Baker. It is unmarked.

Rows to watch:
- 138/139 Milford (Low)/(High): the line '(These two are looked upon as one station).' (line 2460) comes after 139, and I attached it to 139 as a fragment and in `other`. No brace is printed. Both rows name G. Baker.
- 128 North Stack has type 'Fog Horn Station', and 151 'Lundy Fog Gun Station.' has no comma: I split it into name 'Lundy' and type 'Fog Gun Station'. Neither is an L.H. or L.V. 151 and 152 are separate numbered stations, both called Lundy.
- 143 'Nash (Low or W.), L.H.--Wilson.': the dash seems to stand in for a missing first name. The keeper is given as 'Wilson'.
- 124 'Air' is printed as is, presumably Point of Ayr. 'Caldy' (Caldey), 'Flatholm', 'Wolfrock', 'Sevenstones', 'Prichard', 'Syren' and 'Tuskar Buoy' (in 144) are all copied unchanged.
- 'W. Bowen' is the keeper at both 130 Caernarvon Bay L.V. and 154 Trevose Head. That may be two different people.
- 133 Cardigan Bay, 145 Breaksea and 160 Bishop Rock have no keeper printed.
- Keeper names split across two lines: 147 'Amos / Russell' and 150 'Edwd. / Roberts'. Each is given as one name.
- The closing note (line 2496) says light particulars are given only where they were missing from last year's list or have changed. So a row with no character only means nothing new was printed, not that the light has no character.
